claim: In a single-centre RCT of 116 children/adolescents (<=18 y) with drug-resistant epilepsy, 77% of the surgery group vs 7% of the medical-therapy group were seizure free at 12 months; serious adverse events occurred in 33% of the surgery group (hemiparesis 26%). Paediatric-only cohort: analyse separately per protocol.

bibliographic_record.authors: Dwivedi R, Ramanujam B, Chandra PS, Sapra S, Gulati S, et al.
bibliographic_record.title: Surgery for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy in Children

supporting_passage: At 12 months, freedom from seizures occurred in 44 patients (77%) in the surgery group and in 4 (7%) in the medical-therapy group (P<0.001).
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 29069568; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/29069568; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.protocol_flag: pediatric-only cohort -> recorded but analysed separately (protocol exclusion rule)

endpoint.protocol_mapping_v1: seizure freedom -> favourable (Engel/ILAE class not stated in abstract)

reported_observation: 77% vs 7% seizure free at 12 months; 33% serious adverse events in surgery arm.
author_inference: Surgery gave significantly higher seizure freedom and better behaviour and quality of life than continued medical therapy at 12 months.
